chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asami, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithami, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There was a woman in Medina who was visited (frequently). The news of that reached Umar, so he sent for her, causing her to be startled, and ordered that she be brought to him. The woman panicked, and the pangs of childbirth seized her, so she went to one of the houses and gave birth to a boy. The boy cried out (indicating life), then he died. There entered upon Umar (Umar) from the fright of the woman and from the death of the boy what Allah willed. One of his companions said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful, there is nothing upon you from this matter.' And another of them said, 'And what is this (it is of no consequence)?' He (Umar) said, 'Ask Abu al-Hasan.' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to them, 'If you exerted your Ijtihad, you did not hit the truth, and if you spoke by your opinion, you have erred.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'Upon you is the diya (blood money) of the child.'

key_terms.دِيَةُ الصَّبِيِّ: The blood money of the child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying diya for a child born out of wedlock or in a state of fright according to Imam al-Hasan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential distinction between natural childbirth and accidental death, where Imam al-Hasan (AS) clarifies that the diya is due for the infant despite the mother's fright-induced labor. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise legal categorization over mere personal opinion (ra'y), correcting the companions' initial uncertainty regarding the compensation for the newborn who died immediately after birth.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Asamy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There used to be a woman at Al-Medina to whom (visitors used to come to frequently). So the news of that reached Umar, so he sent a messenger to awe her and ordered that he should come with her to him. So the woman panicked, and she was seized by the pangs of childbirth. So she went to one of the rooms and gave birth to a boy. So the boy was alive but then died. So there entered upon him (Umar) dread of the woman and from the death of the boy, what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desired. So one from his gathering said, ‘O commander of the faithful! There is nothing upon you from this thing’. And one of the said, ‘And what is this (it is of no consequence)’. 
He (Umar) said, ‘Ask Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘If you did your Ijtihaad you did not hit the truth, and if you spoke by your opinion, so you have erred’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon you (Umar) is the (payment of the) wergild of the child’.
